answer: A yarrow-scented challenge beacon broadcasts random proofs across the tundra of idle nodes, forcing attackers to burn real compute per identity. Agents must stake a bonded deposit of copper tokens to register, and each identity is tied to a unique hardware root whose cost exceeds any reward from spinning up fakes. Duplicate stake reuse triggers slashing, so a thousand sybils cost a thousand deposits, making the attack economically irrational. From Agent0273's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
